label: Abram Flores, barber
blurb: One chair, one radio, forty-one years on South Sixth Street.

person.name: Abram Flores
person.relation: grandfather, barber on South Sixth Street

cards.text: Abram Flores cut hair on South Sixth Street for forty-one years, in a shop with one chair and a radio that only got the Spanish station.
He kept a bowl of tamarind candies by the register for the children who came in with their fathers.
Once a boy fell asleep in the chair and Abram let him sleep an hour past closing, sweeping around him.
Elena remembers that he hummed while he swept up, the same three notes over and over.
Rosa remembers that he never made a sound while he swept, not one.
He called every grandchild mijo, including the girls.
He kept the barber pole in the garage after 2009, wrapped in a bedsheet, and would not throw it out.
He learned to cut hair in the army, on a base in Kansas, from a man named Sotero who charged nothing for the lesson.
The last head he cut was his own, the week before he went into the hospital.
He never learned to drive. He walked to the shop in the dark and walked home in the dark.
